title: How Much Is a Kilo of Gold Worth?
summary: A kilo of gold is 32.15 troy ounces times the spot price. See the math, a dated example, a real 1 kilo gold bar bid and ask on Pure, and the bar's size.
body_markdown:
A kilo of gold is worth whatever gold is trading at per ounce right now, times 32.15. That's it. When we checked at 5:27 p.m. Pacific on November 25, 2026, the gold price on Pure's site ticker read $3,572 an ounce, which put a kilo at about $114,840 in metal, while the highest bid on a[1 kilo gold bar on Pure](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/kilo-gold-bar-3215-oz-accredited-brand-9999-fine000089) that same minute stood at $114,730.65. Both dollar figures are stale by now. The 32.15 never changes.


## How many troy ounces are in a kilo of gold?


A kilogram is 1,000 grams. No surprise there. The ounce is where it goes sideways, because gold gets priced in[troy ounces](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-is-a-troy-ounce) , which are heavier than the ounce on your kitchen scale,[31.1034768 grams](https://www.nist.gov/pml/special-publication-811/nist-guide-si-appendix-b-conversion-factors/nist-guide-si-appendix-b8) apiece if you want every decimal (a troy ounce is 480 grains with the grain fixed at exactly 64.79891 milligrams, which is where all those digits come from). Divide 1,000 by that. 32.1507. Everybody rounds it to 32.15.


People get this wrong constantly. They grab the everyday 28.35 gram ounce, come up with 35.27 ounces in a kilo, multiply by whatever gold price they saw on the news that morning, then wonder why their number is about $11,000 higher than anybody else's at the price above.


## Working out the price of a kilo of gold


Spot price per troy ounce, times 32.15. That's the metal.


Real numbers. The gold ticker that runs across the top of Pure's site showed two figures at 5:27 p.m. PT on November 25, 2026, $3,572.00 and $3,575.00, so take the first. Times 32.1507 is $114,842.30. Use the rounded 32.15 and you get $114,839.80, two and a half dollars lighter on a six-figure number, so nobody is going to fight you over the rounding.


Grams work too. It's the same sum from the other end, $3,572 divided by 31.1035, which comes to $114.84 a gram. A thousand of those.


Good for maybe a minute, that figure. Gold reprices all day long, so there's no point carrying $114,842 around in your head when you can carry the 32.15, pull up a[live gold price](https://www.collectpure.com/charts/gold) whenever you need the answer, then multiply.


One more thing about[spot](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/what-does-spot-price-mean) . It's the price of the metal itself, in bulk, so a bar you can actually hold gets bought and sold a little above that or a little below it, depending on who's on the other side that day.


## What a 1 kilo gold bar was bid and offered at on Pure


Pure (collectpure.com) is a peer-to-peer marketplace for gold, silver, platinum, palladium and rare coins. Buyers and sellers set their own prices, and a person on our team checks every item before it ships. Every product page shows the highest price a buyer has posted (the bid) next to the least a seller will take right now (the ask). No account needed to see either one.


We opened the[kilo gold bar page](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/kilo-gold-bar-3215-oz-accredited-brand-9999-fine000089) signed out at 5:27 p.m. PT on November 25, 2026. Here's the panel.


Highest bid, $114,730.65. Tagged $4.54 an ounce under spot. Lowest ask, $115,166.79, which the page tagged at $6.02 an ounce over, with a line underneath that read 141 sold on Pure.


Three seconds later we pulled the[1 oz carded gold bar page](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/product/random-brand-1-oz-gold-bar-9999-fine-in-card000087) so there'd be something to hold it against. The highest bid there stood at $3,589.00, tagged $16.00 an ounce over spot, with the lowest ask at $3,604.00 ($28.00 over) and 41,897 sold.


So ounce for ounce the kilo's tags sat closer to spot than the 1 oz bar's that evening, the kilo bid a little under spot where the 1 oz bid was over it. Then look at the sold counts, 141 against 41,897, because that tells you which page has seen more sales.


That's one evening, two pages. Open them yourself first.


Buyers pay no marketplace fee on Pure. Shipping is free on orders of $10,000 or more, which a kilo clears many times over.


## How big is a 1 kilo gold bar?


For something with a six-figure bid on it, a kilo bar is tiny. PAMP's 1 kg cast bar is[115.5 mm long, 52.5 mm wide and 9.2 mm thick](https://www.pamp.com/product/cast-bars/gold-cast-bar-provenance-1-kg) , call it four and a half inches by two with a bit over a third of an inch of depth. The Perth Mint gives its kilo bar as[112 by 52 by 9 mm at the most](https://www.perthmint.com/shop/bullion/cast-bars/1-kilo-gold-cast-bar/) . Shorter and narrower than the phone in your pocket, most likely. 2.2 pounds, though. Gold is just that dense.


Both are cast bars (the gold gets melted and poured into a mold) in .9999 fine gold, which PAMP writes as 999.9 and Perth writes as 99.99%. Perth stamps each one with its swan logo, the weight, the purity, the month and year it was made, plus a serial number.


No assay card on these. The kilo page on Pure says the bars ship uncarded, so what shows up is the bare bar. If you only know 1 oz bars sealed in plastic, we went through[what the card is for](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/sealed-vs-opened-gold-bars) in another post.


A small wrinkle if you read spec sheets. Perth lists the fine gold in its kilo bar as 32.148 troy ounces where you'd expect 32.15. That's the purity talking: 99.99% of a 1,000 gram bar is 999.9 grams of actual gold, which works out to 32.148. About ten dollars' difference at the price above.


## A kilo gold bar vs. a 400 oz bar and a 1 oz bar


The brick in the heist movies is the 400 oz bar. Properly it's the London Good Delivery bar, the one banks trade between themselves, where LBMA's spec lets a single bar hold[350 to 430 troy ounces of gold](https://www.lbma.org.uk/publications/good-delivery-rules/technical-specifications) (roughly 10.9 to 13.4 kilos) at 995 fineness or better. One that lands on exactly 400 ounces is 12.44 kilos, so picture twelve and a half kilo bars melted into one lump, which at $3,572 an ounce is $1,428,800.


Going the other direction, a kilo is 32 one-ounce bars with a sliver left over.


Pure's[gold bar pages](https://www.collectpure.com/marketplace/featured/gold-bars) run from 1 gram up to the kilo. We've got separate posts on[how much gold bars weigh at each size](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-much-does-a-gold-bar-weigh) , on[what a gold bar is worth](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-much-is-a-gold-bar-worth) from the small ones up, plus one on[how the big refiners' bars compare](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/best-gold-bars-for-return-on-investment) . If somebody quoted you gold by the pound, that's a different headache with its own ounce problem, so read[how much a pound of gold is worth](https://www.collectpure.com/blog/how-much-is-a-pound-of-gold-worth) first.

## Questions people ask about a kilo of gold


### How much would $1 million in gold weigh?


About 280 troy ounces at $3,572 an ounce. That's 8.7 kilos, a little over 19 pounds, so not quite nine kilo bars. Shoebox-sized, with room to spare. The weight drops when the gold price is higher and climbs when it's lower, so run it again with today's number.


### What if the gold is 14K or 18K?


Then part of it isn't gold. Karat means parts out of 24, so 18K is 75% gold while 14K is 58.3%. A kilo of 14K chain has about 583 grams of gold in it, call it 18.75 troy ounces, which is the figure you multiply by spot. Bullion kilo bars don't have this problem because they're 999.9 fine.


### Can you sell a kilo gold bar on Pure?


Yes. Pure has a product page for accredited-brand kilo gold bars, linked above. On Pure you can sell into the highest bid, in which case the trade fills right away at that price, or you can post an ask at your own number and wait for a buyer. Pure sends you an insured shipping label at no extra cost. Somebody on our team checks the bar when it comes in, then payout is automatic about 3 business days after check-in. Seller fees range from 0.5% to 1.5%.
